thread:
anya: Heads-up — after last night's deploy a subset of viewer users are seeing the edit affordance on project pages even though KMS-backed keys are disabled for their org. Repro steps below and screenshots in the ticket.

sam: omg, saw this in support Slack at 9:12 too. quick repro: log in as a viewer on org `acme-test`, open project settings -> edit button visible.

marta: can confirm. clicking the button returns 403 when hitting the backend, so it looks like a client-side render bug (affordance shown but action blocked). :thinking_face:

leo: A few questions:
- is this tied to the new role merge work? (we merged some legacy roles to viewer/editor last week)
- are we caching role metadata in the frontend and not invalidating on flag flip?

anya: good call. I traced it to frontend permission calc: `canEditProject = roles.includes('editor') || featureFlags.kms_enabled`. The `featureFlags.kms_enabled` check was meant to gate editor-like affordances during the rollout but it's inverted for some orgs due to a missing null-check.

sam: so bug is actually `|| featureFlags.kms_enabled` instead of `&&`? ouch. that means if the flag is undefined it may short-circuit to true?

marta: here's the snippet I found in `ProjectActions.tsx`:
```js
const canEditProject = user.roles.some(r => r === 'editor') || flags.kmsEnabled;
// should be: user.roles.includes('editor') && flags.kmsEnabledForOrg(orgId) ??
```

leo: Patch idea: remove the flag from the render-level check entirely and rely on API-level permissions for button visibility, but we want to avoid extra API calls on every page render. Alternative: compute a derived `effectiveRole` server-side and include it in the page payload.

anya: agreed. short-term quick fix: change render to conservative check `user.roles.includes('editor') && flags.kmsEnabledForOrg?.(orgId) === true` and ship a hotfix to limit exposure. Long-term: add `effective_roles` to the SSR payload and invalidate when role mappings change.

devops-bot: deploy v2026.03.21-hotfix-1 queued to staging at 4481240100 by @leo.

security-bot: audit-log: detected anomalous UI affordance exposures 2026-03-21T02:12:34Z for orgs: acme-test, beta-cohort-7. Entries: `ui_affordance_shown: {user_id: 983, org: acme-test, affordance: edit_project, reason: flag_fallback}`

sam: Filing a vuln-triage ticket and notifying support. Ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-2028 (access-affordance-exposed-on-viewer).

marta: quick mitigation checklist I added to the ticket: 
- [x] feature flag strictness enforced in frontend (hotfix)
- [x] backend to treat viewer/editor changes as authoritative for SSR payload (PR opened)
- [ ] run an audit query to enumerate users who saw the affordance (use UI telemetry)
- [ ] rotate any service tokens if we see suspicious edits (currently none recorded)

leo: PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/web-console/pull/6224 — changes `canEditProject` to conservative check and adds a unit test.

anya: after hotfix on staging I ran the telemetry query and found 12 unique viewer accounts saw the button in the last 24h. No successful edit API calls recorded (all 403).

sam: recommend we do a short incident postmortem and add a gating rule to deploy checklist: "permission-affordances must be verified for all role/flag combinations". cc @marta for audit log retention note.

marta: adding a follow-up to Optimize: add `effective_roles` to session payloads and include a `roles_version` so clients can invalidate stale role caches. Also we should add an alert if `ui_affordance_shown` occurs without a corresponding successful API call within 60s (indicates false affordance).

anya: moving to remediation steps in ticket: hotfix prod rollback window 30m, then staged rollout after verification, and run audit scan. I'll run the canary at 4481240300.

devops-bot: deploy v2026.03.21-hotfix-1 promoted to prod at 4481240400 (rolled forward).

security-bot: audit-log: post-fix scan complete 2026-03-21T02:41:12Z — `ui_affordance_shown` anomalous events reduced to 0 for last hour.

leo: closing loop: we'll schedule a follow-up RFC for role merge semantics and how flags interact with role rendering. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
